description.narrative:
Aegis Trust har i samarbete med Radio La Benevolencija (RLB) ansökt om finansiering till insatsen Aegis Trust 2021-2025 'Action for Sustainable Peace, Inclusion, Rights & Equality (ASPIRE)'. Varaktigheten för programmet löper från 29 november 2021 till 29 november 2025 med en budget på 70 miljoner SEK.
Insatsens syftar till att förbättra förutsättningarna för en hållbar fred i Rwanda genom Freds och Värderingsutbildning (hädanefter refererad till som PVE, vilket står för Peace and Value Education) och samhällsdialog för att öka förståelsen för de grundläggande orsakerna och händelserna som ledde fram till folkmordet mot tutsierna 1994 samt bygga empati, motståndskraft och mod att motverka etniska splittringar, våld och hat. Det föreslagna programmet bygger vidare på en tidigare insats, Education for Sustainable Peace Rwanda (ESPR), 2016-2021, finansierad av ambassaden, som implementerades tillsammans med RLB. Med den föreslagna insatsen vill Aegis Trust och RLB utöka och förbättra kvaliteten på och implementeringen av Peace and Values Education (PVE). En starkare tonvikt läggs på behovet av PVE i samhällsutrymmen för att även nå ut till ungdomar som inte går i skolan men även för att föra dialog och stärka förmågan och viljan att diskutera dessa frågor i hemmiljön såväl som inom samhället. Insatsen har ett fortsatt starkt fokus på att stärka kapaciteten och resurserna bland lärare att implementera PVE som en övergripande del av den nationella läroplanen.

Aegis Trust, in partnership with Radio La Benevolencija (RLB) has submitted to the Embassy a proposal for a four-year programme titled, ’Action for Sustainable Peace, Inclusion, Rights & Equality (ASPIRE)’. The proposed duration of the programme is 29 November 2021 to 29 November 2025, and the budget is 70 million SEK. The proposed programme aims to build positive peace through Peace and Value Education (PVE) and community dialogue to increase an understanding of the root causes and events that lead up to the Genocide against the Tutsi in 1994 while simultaneously building empathy, resilience, and courage to counteract ethnic divisions, violence and hatred. The proposed programme expands on previous work by Aegis Trust and its cooperation partner Radio La Benevolencija (RLB) conducted as part of the Education for Sustainable Peace Rwanda (ESPR), 2016-2021, funded by the Embassy, but the proposed programme has an increased focus on community dialogue, out-of-schoolyouth, and better resourced teachers able to fully implement PVE as a cross-cutting issue part of the national curriculum. The programme will be solely funded by the Embassy of Sweden but complemented by the “Ubumuntu” digital platform funded by the Embassy of Belgium. Ubumuntu is an online gateway for teachers, parents, students, youth, and decision makers to access educational resources for PVE. It complements this programme by enabling a digital resource that can be used by teachers, village leaders and both programme and non-programme participants to refresh knowledge learn about PVE from scratch. During the latter half of 2021, the Embassy of Belgium has issued new project for this , which will cover funding for the next three years to a total of one million EURO. This resource can help strengthen activities at the community level and within schools depending on access to digital devices and internet connection.
The proposed contribution’s overarching objective is to OContribute to building the conditions for a peaceful, cohesive and inclusive society’ through working directly with teachers, parents, youth, and decision makers. Through PVE, Aegis Trust and its cooperation partner RLB seeking to achieve the following outcomes: Outcome 1: Teachers and School leaders understand, recognize and can teach about processes that lead to identify-based violence; they have developed positive social and emotional skills and are able to incorporate teaching these into their educative practice. Outcome 2: Youth develop their critical thinking, social and emotional skills, and positive values. This leads to them understanding, identifying and counteracting processes that lead to social divisions and identity-based violence, taking personal responsibility for the impact of their thoughts, speech and behaviour on themselves and others, better managing their own mental health and wellbeing, and better resolving conflicts with peers, family and others. Outcome 3: Parents experience positive personal change and greater inner peace and social trust, and develop a personal commitment to principles on non-violence, inclusion, and being active by-standers. Outcome 4: Decision-makers engage with research based-evidence informing their policies and practice. The underlying assumptions are that critical thinking, empathy, trust and conflict resolution skills are powerful tools to prevent and counteract Osocial and psychosocial processes’ identity-based hatred and violence.

description.narrative:
Under Each program pillar a summary of the achievements are registered through ASPIRE's boundary partners as follow.
Boundary Partner 1: School Leaders and Teachers.
This category of boundary partners includes preservice teachers Teacher Training Colleges (TTC) tutors Inservice teachers School leaders and Education officers in sectors. The program continued equipping Teachers and School leaders (men and women) to understand, recognize, and teach about processes that lead to identity based violence. This effort developed positive social and emotional skills which as a result enabled the teachers to incorporate teaching these into their educative practice. The teachers were able to understand the value of, and are now personally committed to promoting, inclusion, human rights, and equality. In the implementation year of 2024, ASPIRE continued to contribute to the improvement of the delivery of peace education within the current Competence based curriculum in Rwandan schools responding to a set of progress makers designed using Outcome mapping.
Some of the outputs registered in this period include: Nine workshops trained 319 preservice teachers (57% male, 43% female) at Kayonza Districts URCE Rukara Campus from February 19 to March 25, 2024. Ten workshops were conducted, training 258 in-service teachers (149 males, 109 females) and including 41 school leaders representing ASPIRE Community Peace Centers (CPC). Two training sessions on Peace and Values Education (PVE) were conducted gathering 68 Teacher Training College (TTC) tutors (76% male, 24% female) from all TTCs across the country.
Boundary Partner 2: Parents
ASPIRE focuses on two groups of parents namely representatives of Parent Teacher Associations (PTAs) from schools already engaged in PVE training and parents from families living in conflict, selected at the sector level. In 2024 ASPIRE continued to strongly recognize the role of parents in building a culture of peace in families and communities and in their quality of role models for their children. In the framework of ASPIRE, the parents portrayed positive personal change with greater inner peace and social trust, and to have a developed personal commitment to principles of nonviolence, inclusion. The Peace Values Education training has managed to equip participants with the knowledge, skills, methodologies, and attitudes needed to deliver Peace and Values Education effectively, both in classrooms and in the community. During the reported period, ASPIRE equipped parents with knowledge, skills, methodology and attitudes that helps them deliver Peace and Values Education in their homes and community. Some of the outputs registered under this pillar are Six workshops were conducted with 152 parents (53% male, 47% female) to empower them with the knowledge and skills necessary for promoting positive family dynamics and contribute to sustainable peace. Three mental health awareness workshops were organized, gathering 101 Youth (53% M and 47%). Participants were equipped with practical mental health skills encouraging them to work toward healthy and safe minds.
Boundary Partner 3: Youth
Within the framework of ASPIRE, Aegis Trust continued to conduct youth champions' programme crafted to equip targeted young individuals with essential skills, positive values, resources, and ongoing support. This enabled the youth to comprehend, identify, and effectively counteract processes that contribute to violence within their communities. Outputs registered under this pillar include the following: Three training sessions were conducted on Peace and Values Education, involving 72 youth (49% male, 51% female). Participants were also introduced to the Ubumuntu Digital Platform, which provides accessible peacebuilding content, enabling them to share the knowledge gained from the training with their peers. A two days workshop on Non Violent Communication was organized with 38 young influencers including digital creators, journalists, and artists (63% male, 37% female and 1 person living with disability). This training was aimed at equipping young influencers with necessary skills to integrate peace and values into their work, countering the rise of hate speech, genocide denialism, and online violence. Participants have now acquired deeper insights into genocide related issues and have reflected on the training as an opportunity for healing, forgiveness, and supporting each other's mental wellbeing. This is assessed to be very vital especially for the youth of Rwanda today who are most at risk to be indoctrinated with hate and intergenerational trauma that can set back the efforts that has been made in promoting sustainable peace and unity in the country.
Boundary Partner 4: Researchers and Decision Makers
The program ASPIRE continues to equip Researchers with the expertise required to carry out quality Peace related research in a multidisciplinary fashion using quantitative, qualitative, and/or participatory methodologies with special emphasis on gender specificities. Researchers have managed to provide credible evidence that allow research findings to be translated into effective policies and programs and to skillfully disseminate research results in appropriate format for respective audience. Researchers have also managed to create relationships with donor communities for further research and have also been mentors for young upcoming researchers in the field. This has managed to create relationships between Rwandan researchers with more experienced peace building researchers, globally for mentorship and exchange. Decision makers will uptake research based evidence generated by ASPIRE and use it in policy making and peace building practice.
The Genocide Research Hub is considered as a critical source of information on genocide and post genocide peacebuilding and reconstruction strategies. By building local research capacity, ASPIRE empowers Rwandans not only to own their history but also to shape the narratives from a Rwandan perspective. Some of the outputs noted under this pillar are highlighted below.
In May 2024 Aegis Trust through the program ASPIRE launched a call for concept notes on research to the Genocide Research Hub. The research proposals for the recruitment of Cohort III research grantees attracted 23 research papers (39% F 61% M). Five research projects were funded involving 7 researchers (2 Rwandans and 5 internationals). Another key output was capacity building sessions for research grantees. Junior or midcareer researchers from diverse fields of social sciences, practitioners and highly motivated postgraduate students attended a two day Capacity Strengthening Workshop under the theme The fundamentals of social science knowledge production, dissemination & uptake. The workshop focused on the following key dimensions: Understanding and contextualizing research in social sciences Qualitative and quantitative research methods The Use of theory in social science research and conducting literature review Field research and data analysis Publication and dissemination of Research Conducting Research for Policy Dialogues and Writing for academic and nonacademic audiences. On output level , 43 individuals(37% F 63% M) including Aegis Trust research grantees were trained.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
